entity.summary: Corporations, S corporations and LLCs doing business in Illinois must register with the Illinois Secretary of State.
entity.quote: If you are conducting business in Illinois and choose to organize as a corporation, an S corporation, or an LLC, you must register with the Illinois Secretary of State.

state_tax.summary: Register with the Department of Revenue (Form REG-1, online through MyTax Illinois) before you make purchases or sales or hire an employee.
state_tax.quote: Register with us, using one of the above methods, before you make any purchases, sales, or hire an employee.

unemployment.summary: Employers can register with IDES for unemployment insurance through MyTax Illinois when they register with the Department of Revenue.
unemployment.quote: If necessary, you may also register with the Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) using MyTax Illinois.

workers_comp.summary: Not confirmed from an official page: the Commission's site loads its content by script and the statute host (ilga.gov) failed a TLS check. Roofing contractors with employees must prove workers' comp coverage to get licensed.

residential_building.covers: General and residential contractors are not licensed by the state; check with your city or county.
residential_building.summary: Illinois has no state general or residential contractor license; the state licensing agency's list of regulated professions has none. Check your city or county for local licensing, and note that roofing and plumbing are licensed by the state.
residential_building.quote: Professions and Industries regulated by IDFPR are organized below alphabetically for your convenience.
residential_building.note: Absence from IDFPR's profession list; Illinois statutes on ilga.gov could not be fetched (TLS certificate error) to cite municipal licensing authority. The Attorney General's Home Repair and Remodeling guidance applies to consumer contracts.

commercial_building.covers: Commercial general contractors are not licensed by the state.
commercial_building.summary: There is no state commercial general contractor license in Illinois; licensing, if any, is local.
commercial_building.quote: Professions and Industries regulated by IDFPR are organized below alphabetically for your convenience.
commercial_building.note: Based on absence from IDFPR's profession list.

electrical.covers: Electrical contractors and electricians are not licensed by the state.
electrical.summary: Illinois does not issue a state electrician or electrical contractor license; many cities and counties license electrical contractors locally.
electrical.quote: Professions and Industries regulated by IDFPR are organized below alphabetically for your convenience.
electrical.note: Based on absence from IDFPR's profession list; the municipal licensing statute on ilga.gov could not be fetched.

plumbing.name: Illinois Plumber license, Apprentice Plumber license, Plumbing Contractor registration
plumbing.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), Plumbing Program
plumbing.covers: Plumbers, apprentices, and any licensed plumber doing work for another person (plumbing contractor).
prerequisites: At least 4 years as a licensed apprentice plumber
At least 2 years of high school (or equivalent) plus approved course instruction
Contractor: general liability, bodily injury, property damage and workers' compensation insurance
plumbing.insurance: Plumbing contractors: general liability, bodily injury, property damage and workers' compensation insurance
plumbing.summary: Plumbers in Illinois need a state license from IDPH, earned after years as a licensed apprentice and passing the exam. Plumbers who work for others must also register as plumbing contractors and carry liability and workers' comp insurance.
plumbing.quote: Under the Illinois Plumbing License Law (225 ILCS 320), the Department licenses plumbers, plumbing contractors, plumbers’ apprentices, irrigation contractors and retired plumbers.
plumbing.note: The City of Chicago issues its own plumber licenses with a reciprocity path.

evidence.quote: Applicants must have been employed as a licensed apprentice plumber for a minimum of 4 years, and have successfully completed at least 2 years of high school or equivalent in addition to completing an approved course instruction through a college, university or trade school.
Plumbing contractors must maintain minimum general liability insurance, bodily injury insurance, property damage insurance, and worker’s compensation insurance.

mechanical.covers: HVAC contractors are not licensed by the state.
mechanical.summary: Illinois has no state HVAC license; check local requirements.
mechanical.quote: Professions and Industries regulated by IDFPR are organized below alphabetically for your convenience.
mechanical.note: Based on absence from IDFPR's profession list.

roofing.name: Roofing Contractor license, Limited (residential) or Unlimited, with a Qualifying Party
roofing.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR)
roofing.covers: Roofing contractors; Limited covers residential roofing (8 units or less), Unlimited adds commercial and industrial.
prerequisites: Designate a qualifying party who passes the Illinois Residential or Residential/Commercial/Industrial exam
Proof of workers' compensation insurance (if you have employees)
IDES statement showing an unemployment insurance account in good standing (if you have employees)
Liability and property damage insurance (form RF-INS)
Surety bond on the Department's bond form
roofing.bond: Surety bond from a bonding company licensed in Illinois (Limited or Unlimited bond form)
roofing.insurance: Liability and property damage insurance, plus workers' compensation if you have employees
roofing.summary: Roofing contractors need a state license from IDFPR. The business must name a qualifying party who passes the state roofing exam, and must submit proof of liability insurance, a surety bond, and, if it has employees, workers' comp and an unemployment insurance account.
roofing.quote: This person must take and pass either the Illinois Residential Examination or the Illinois Residential, Commercial and Industrial Examination. A qualifying party is required for any roofing contractor license in Illinois.

evidence.quote: Limited Roofing License means a license made available to contractors whose roofing business is limited to residential roofing, including residential properties consisting of 8 units or less.
Proof of worker's compensation insurance for roofing which must be in the form of a Certificate of Insurance from the insurance provider
Supporting Document RF-INS must be properly completed and submitted. This is the only proof of liability and property damage insurance which will be accepted by this Department.
must be properly completed and submitted by a bonding company licensed to do business within the State of Illinois.
A Statement of Account from the Illinois Department of Employment Security indicating

pesticide.name: Commercial Pesticide Applicator / Operator license (IDOA); Structural Pest Control license (IDPH)
pesticide.agency: Illinois Department of Agriculture; Illinois Department of Public Health (structural pest control)
pesticide.covers: Anyone who purchases, uses or supervises use of general or restricted use pesticides for hire (lawn, tree, weed control). Pest control in and on buildings is licensed by IDPH.
prerequisites: Pass the General Standards exam (70 or more) and category exams
Certificate of insurance (financial responsibility) for commercial applicators
At least one licensed applicator at each facility location
pesticide.insurance: Certificate of insurance showing financial responsibility for personal injury and property damage
pesticide.summary: Lawn care, tree and weed-control companies applying pesticides for hire need IDOA commercial applicator/operator licenses: pass the state exams, show insurance, and keep a licensed applicator at each location. Structural pest control (insects, rodents in buildings) is licensed separately by IDPH.
pesticide.quote: Commercial Applicator or Operator License - required for individuals who purchase, use or supervise the use of pesticides classified for General or Restricted Use for hire.

evidence.quote: Pass the 100-question General Standards exam or Aerial General Standards exam with a score of 70 or more.
commercial applicators must provide a certificate of insurance with proper coverage.
Each organization must have at least one person licensed as an applicator at each facility location.
The Illinois Department of Public Health certifies and licenses individuals applying pesticides in and on man-made structures.

asbestos.name: Asbestos Abatement Contractor, Supervisor and Worker licenses
asbestos.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health, Lead and Asbestos Licensing Unit
asbestos.covers: Contractors conducting asbestos abatement projects in schools and commercial or public buildings, and their trained workers and supervisors.
prerequisites: Trained and licensed workers and supervisors
asbestos.summary: Asbestos abatement contractors in Illinois must be licensed by IDPH and carry insurance, and their workers must be trained and licensed.
asbestos.quote: All contractors who conduct asbestos abatement projects must have insurance and are required to be licensed.

evidence.quote: Workers who manage or abate asbestos in schools, commercial, or public buildings must be trained and licensed.

lead_rrp.name: EPA Lead-Safe Certified Firm and Certified Renovator
lead_rrp.covers: Anyone paid to disturb paint in homes, child care facilities and preschools built before 1978.
lead_rrp.summary: Illinois is not on EPA's list of authorized RRP programs, so renovation firms get lead-safe certification directly from EPA.
lead_rrp.quote: EPA administers the RRP Program in most Tribes, states and territories, but has authorized the following to operate their own programs: Alabama, Delaware, Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Massachusetts, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin
lead_rrp.note: IDPH separately licenses lead abatement (not RRP) professionals.

evidence.quote: EPA's RRP Rule requires that anyone paid to perform work that disturbs painted surfaces in homes, childcare facilities and preschools built before 1978 be certified and their employees be trained

other.name: Irrigation Contractor registration
other.summary: Contractors who install lawn sprinkler systems must register with IDPH every year.
other.quote: Each irrigation contractor in the state of Illinois must register annually with the Department
